div.head: III Eg 3
div.ab: ⁊ se dema, se ðe oðrum on woh gedeme, gesylle þam cynge hundtwelfti scill' to bote – butan he mid aðe gecyðan durre, þæt he hit na rihtor ne cuðe – ⁊ þolige á his þegnscipes, butan he hine eft æt þam cynge gebigge, swa he him geðafian wille; ⁊ ámanige þære scyr biscop þa bote to ðæs cynges handa.

⁊ se déma, þe oðrum woh deme, gesylle þam cinge hundtwelftig scill' to bote — butan he mid aðe cyþan durre, þæt he hit na rihtor ne cuðe — ⁊ ðolige áa his ðegnscypes, butan he hine æt þam cynge gebicge, swa swa he him geðafian wille; ⁊ amanige þære scyre bisceop þa bote to ðæs cynges handa.

… twelftig scill' to bote — butan he hit mid aðe gecyþan durre, þæt he hit na rihtor ne cuðe — ⁊ þolie áá his þegenscipes, butan he hine æt þam cynge gebicge, swa he him þafian wille; ⁊ ofmanige þære scire biscop þa bote to ðæs cynges handa.
Et iudex qui iudicium iniustum iudicabit alicui, det regi CXX sol., nisi iurare audeat, quod rectius nesciuit; et admanniat scyre presul emendam illam ad manum regis.

[Be unrihtum dome.] [Ld] ⁊ se dema, þe oðrum woh deme, gesille þam cynge hundtwelftig scill' to bote—buton he mid aðe gecyðan durre, þæt he hit na rihtor ne cuðe—⁊ þolige áá his þegenscipes, buton he hine æt ðam cynge gebicge, swa he him geþafian wille; ⁊ ofmanige scirebiscop þa bote to ðæs cynges handa.

And se dema, se ðe oðrum on woh gedeme, gesylle þam cynge hundtwelfti scillinga to bote—butan he mid aðe gecyðan durre þæt he hit na rihtor ne cuðe—and þolige a his þegnscipes, butan he hine eft æt þam cynge gebigge, swa he him geðafian wille; and amanige þære scyre biscop þa bote to ðæs cynges handa.

And a judge who gives a false judgment against another man shall pay 120 shillings as compensation to the king, unless he is prepared to declare on oath that he did not know how to give a more just decision; and he shall forfeit for ever his rank as a thegn, unless he redeem it from the king on such terms as the king will allow him. And the bishop of the diocese shall exact the compensation on the king's behalf.

And a judge who rules unjustly against another must give one hundred twenty shillings to the king as compensation—unless he is confident enough to declare on oath that he did not know how to rule more justly—and forfeit forever his status as thane, unless he redeems it from the king in such a manner as the latter will permit him; and the bishop of the diocese shall exact the fine on the king’s behalf.

And the judge who pronounces a wrong judgment on another is to pay to the king 120 shillings as compensation, unless he dare declare on oath that he knew not how to do it more justly- and he is always to forfeit his thegnly status, unless he may redeem it from the king, according as he will allow him. And the bishop of the diocese is to exact the compensation on the king’s behalf.

(Von ungerechtem Urtheil. Ld) Und der Richter, welcher jemandem (in G) Ungerechtigkeit zuerkennt, zahle dem König 120 Schilling als Busse — ausser wenn er durch Eid zu beweisen wagt, dass er es nicht richtiger wusste —, und verliere immer seine Thegnwürde [sammt Gerichtshoheit], ausser wenn er sie (wieder G) vom Könige auslöst, so wie dieser ihm zu gestatten geruht; und es fordere der Diöcesanbischof diese Busse zu des Königs Gunsten ein.

(Of unjust judgment. Ld) And the judge who awards injustice to another (in, G) [judgment], let him pay the king 120 shillings as compensation — unless he dares to declare on oath that he did not know how to do it more justly — and let him lose his thegnly rank [together with his jurisdiction] for ever, unless he buys it back (again, G) from the king, as the king is willing to permit him; and let the bishop of the shire exact the compensation on the king's behalf.
div.note: G2 (Nero A I f. 89, c. 1060) begins here at ‘…twelftig scill’ to bote’. Liebermann compares II As 25.1. G2 is in another hand than G and was originally a separate part of the manuscript; Liebermann prints it as a fourth column to the end of III Eg (pp. 201–207).

literally, “his thegnship”, which normally means “the rank and privileges of a thegn”. This word was probably chosen here instead of folgað “office”, as a term which could apply to holders of private jurisdictions as well as appointed officials.
